biophysical_burden.boundary: Service gap combines availability, accessibility and quality; it is not a plant-downtime count.

transformations.formula: Subtract JMP safely managed drinking-water coverage from 100 percent.
Normalize only the top-level population lacking safely managed service; do not add nested service categories.
Divide countries with safely managed estimates by 193 UN Member States.

receipts.uncertainty: Safely managed service requires accessibility, availability and freedom from contamination; national monitoring coverage and modeled estimates vary. The gap does not isolate hydrologic supply, treatment plant capacity or raw-water quality.
receipts.freshness: Reviewed global assessment as of 2024; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T22:18:24.717Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: WHO/UNICEF quantifies the global safely managed drinking-water gap, affected population, 24-year persistence and country coverage.
higher_priority_failures: The report does not provide a complete annual global treatment-plant exceedance or downtime series.
The service gap is therefore accumulated impact rather than a current operational treatment score.

biophysical_burden.boundary: Non-revenue water combines physical and apparent losses.

extent.geography: Global public-water utility non-revenue water estimate

transformations.formula: Normalize the World Bank global annual volume without relabeling it as leakage.
Normalize the separate global annual waste and foregone-revenue estimate.
Use elapsed years since the reviewed estimate as a conservative persistence floor.
Use full extent for the source-reported global public-utility estimate.

receipts.uncertainty: The estimate is older and combines physical losses, meter error, illegal connections and unbilled authorized use. Utility coverage, exchange rates and valuation methods vary.
receipts.freshness: Reviewed global assessment as of 2018; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T22:18:24.761Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: World Bank quantifies global non-revenue-water volume, economic loss, persistent burden and global utility scope.
higher_priority_failures: No method-comparable 20-year annual global non-revenue-water series is available.
The assessment does not separate physical leakage from apparent and commercial losses.
